description: §19.16.3 rule 1 (S430 round 4, N3) — a function DECLARED inside a deferred body is its own control-flow scope: its own `!{}` (not total — only `::Busy`) keeps the unmatched-error propagation. risky() fails with Gone, `inner` returns that error (it does NOT run on to "past;"), and the deferred body's total handler records "inner-failed;". trace = "work;inner-failed;" — identical to the no-defer twin. (Before the fix the deferred-body flag leaked into `inner`, its propagation was dropped, and it appended "past;".)
rationale: §19.16.3 rule 1: a function nested inside a deferred body is its own control-flow scope; only the deferred body itself is restricted.
